query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but inadequate oxygen resistance prevents most practical high-temperature applications. Earlier oxidation-protection research prevented pesting in a related, non-equiatomic Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr alloy during a 5 h exposure to air at 800 °C, but that result does not establish protection for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr; related studies on other refractory alloys likewise did not evaluate this composition. With preservation of useful room- and high-temperature mechanical performance as a design constraint, what single intervention could improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr? Formulate one hypothesis identifying the intervention and mechanism, predicting the outcome relative to untreated material, defining the applicable temperature, atmosphere, exposure-time, and loading boundaries, citing supporting evidence from the prior studies, and specifying a controlled experiment and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a pack aluminization treatment to equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr will improve its oxygen resistance by forming a thin, adherent Al2O3 scale, thereby limiting oxygen ingress without degrading its intrinsic room‐ and high‐temperature mechanical performance.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr with 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C under strain rates of 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹, but displaying inadequate oxygen resistance.
generation.intervention: A pack aluminization treatment in which the alloy surface is exposed to an Al-rich powder mixture at elevated temperature to induce surface Al diffusion.
generation.conditions: Exposure to static air at approximately 800 °C for up to 5 hours, with subsequent mechanical performance evaluated at room temperature and during high-temperature (≈1000 °C) application at strain rates of 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of a continuous, adherent Al2O3 surface scale on the treated alloy.
generation.mechanism: During high-temperature exposure, the diffused Al reacts preferentially with oxygen to form a stable Al2O3 layer. This scale acts as a robust diffusion barrier that prevents further oxygen ingress into the bulk alloy and thus minimizes oxidation-induced degradation, while the limited penetration of the treatment leaves the bulk’s ductility and high-temperature strength largely unaffected.
generation.predicted_outcome: The treated HfNbTaTiZr should show significantly reduced mass gain and slower oxide scale growth during high-temperature air exposure, with room-temperature ductility and high-temperature yield strength remaining comparable to the untreated alloy.
generation.baseline: The untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr alloy exhibits inadequate oxygen resistance marked by rapid oxidation, despite retaining useful mechanical performance.
generation.boundary: The anticipated benefits apply for exposures in air at around 800 °C for durations up to 5 hours; the treatment must not introduce any detrimental phase changes in the substrate that would compromise mechanical performance at room temperature or at 1000 °C.
generation.uncertainty: While the general protective effect of an Al2O3 scale is well established, the precise kinetics of scale formation, the optimal processing parameters for maintaining bulk properties, and the long-term stability of the treated surface under cyclic or dynamic loading conditions remain to be quantified.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate a set of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr specimens and apply a pack aluminization treatment to half of them under controlled processing conditions. Expose both treated and untreated specimens to static air at 800 °C for 5 hours. After exposure, use scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and X-ray diffraction (XRD) to characterize the oxide scale, and perform mass gain measurements as a proxy for oxidation extent. Conduct standardized tensile tests at room temperature and yield strength tests at 1000 °C.
measurements: Oxide scale composition and thickness (via SEM/XRD)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the pack aluminized specimens do not exhibit a statistically significant reduction in mass gain and form a continuous, protective Al2O3 layer compared to untreated samples, or if their ductility and high-temperature strength are notably degraded, then the hypothesis is falsified.

Paper card. Question: Can high-entropy alloys be designed to simultaneously achieve high Snoek-type damping capacity, high mechanical strength, and high ductility at elevated temperatures?. System: Ta0.5Nb0.5HfZrTi base HEA, (Ta0.5Nb0.5HfZrTi)98O2 (O-2 HEA), and (Ta0.5Nb0.5HfZrTi)98N2 (N-2 HEA). Processing: Arc-melting of pure metals (purity >99.9 wt%), TiN (99.9 wt%), and TiO2 (99.9 wt%) in a Ti-gettered high-purity argon atmosphere; remelted at least eight times; drop-cast into a water-cooled copper mold (10 mm × 10 mm × 60 mm). Test conditions: Damping measured via multifunction internal friction apparatus at 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, and 4.0 Hz, temperature range 300–1100 K, heating rate 2 K min⁻¹, max strain amplitude 2 × 10⁻⁴; Tensile tests at room temperature, strain rate 1 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹. Paper card. Question: How does an ultrafine-grain microstructure, obtained via stationary friction processing, affect the oxidation behavior of AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy?. System: Equimolar AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy (HEA). Processing: Stationary friction processing (SFP) using a WC-cylindrical tool (12 mm diameter) at rotational speeds of 400 rpm and 1800 rpm for 5 min duration. Test conditions: Isothermal oxidation in laboratory air at 850, 950, and 1050 °C for 100 h. Question: Can refractory high-entropy alloy WTaMoNbV be adequately synthesized via a laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) process using mixed elemental alloying powder as the raw material, and how do its properties compare to a counterpart produced by arc melting furnace (AMF)?. System: Refractory High-Entropy Alloy WTaMoNbV (20 at.% W, 20 at.% Ta, 20 at.% Mo, 20 at.% Nb, 20 at.% V). Processing: Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) using EOSINT M290 system (400 W Nd-YAG laser, pure argon atmosphere); mixed elemental powders (20–70 µm) stirred for 6 h at 23 rpm; advanced trials parameters: 244 W laser power, 300 mm/s scanning speed, 0.10 mm hatch spacing, 0.03 mm layer thickness, 162.7 J/mm³ energy density, 67° layer rotation..
